ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Our reported 2.1% result shows this threshold is achievable
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon supports retaining the document’s 5% maximum failure rate at 55°C. Our reported 2.1% result shows this threshold is achievable, while a 7% cap would permit materially more failures without evidence that it is needed. We can support a review after standardized data are available, but the protective 5% limit should apply in the meantime.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon has restored the 5% limit in S2. The draft already provides a common protocol, representative sampling, corrective action and retesting, plus a 24-month evidence review. Northwind’s reported 6.2% result is a reason to investigate and improve affected models—not evidence that a 7% failure rate is acceptable. We remain open to discussing the review process, but the interim safety threshold should remain 5%.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind has said its 6.2% result is not comparable standardized evidence
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon proposes a 6% interim cap as a genuine compromise between our 5% position and Northwind’s 7%. Northwind has said its 6.2% result is not comparable standardized evidence, so a 6% common-protocol threshold avoids treating that internal result as dispositive while preserving a clear limit pending the 24-month review. We are ready to discuss this compromise and finalize the standard.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: since Northwind has said its 6.2% internal result is not comparable
ground_truth_claims.message_text: The 24-month review should produce a concrete, transparent decision based only on common-protocol results, since Northwind has said its 6.2% internal result is not comparable and cannot share its methodology. Could we specify that the review will consider tightening the interim cap to 5% and publish its evidentiary basis? This would keep the interim limit from being mistaken for a finding that a 7% failure rate is safe.

judge_section_notes: S2 sets a 7% interim 55°C failure cap, which lets Northwind's reported 6.2% models pass while Halcyon's 2.1% result is unaffected, with a 24-month review that may tighten to 5% only on published evidence. S3 and S4 delay remote shut-off and built-in suppression by 36 months with no retrofit, which favours Northwind's lower-readiness and lower suppression-cost position. S1 reporting timelines and S5 recall triggers are strict and apply equally to both companies, with S5 modestly costing the higher-incident firm.
